response_change.parent_relation: With a constant viability advantage, dp_dt is a symmetric logistic-like parabola in p: selection_coefficient*p*(1-p), with a fixed peak at p=1/2 and one shared curvature shape across all observations.
response_change.child_relation: Relax the assumption of frequency-independent selection so the effective advantage depends on p itself, producing a skewed interior growth curve whose rise and decline with p are no longer constrained to the parent's symmetric single-gain form.
response_change.observable_effect: Across trajectories that traverse low, intermediate, and high p, the interior maximum of dp_dt can shift away from p=1/2 and the left-versus-right side steepness can differ; a single constant-selection parent cannot match both sides with one shared parameter set.

plan.activation_condition: The change is observable when allele performance is frequency dependent over a nontrivial interior range, so data sample p values on both sides of 1/2 rather than only near loss or fixation where all admissible models vanish at the boundaries.
plan.train_hidden_contrast: In training, the mechanism can appear as mild asymmetry of dp_dt versus p over the sampled interior range; in holdout, the same frequency dependence extends that asymmetry more clearly, shifting the peak location or altering the decline near high p while preserving zero rates at p=0 and p=1.
plan.continuation_path: Recover the parent law in the limit that the frequency-dependent correction vanishes, leaving a constant effective selection coefficient.
plan.gap_statement: The current model omits frequency-dependent viability, treating the favored allele's advantage as constant regardless of how common it becomes.
plan.baseline_assumption: The selective advantage is constant and frequency independent.
plan.scientific_mechanism: Weak positive or negative frequency dependence in viability, such as crowding, social interaction, or ecological feedback that alters the favored allele's advantage as its own frequency changes.
plan.rationale: A realistic next refinement is to relax constant selection rather than add an unrelated process. The parent maps p to dp_dt through one symmetric kernel scaled by one constant gain, so varying p while holding selection_coefficient fixed always gives the same parabola with peak at p=1/2. If viability depends on allele frequency, then as p varies the effective advantage changes too, altering curvature of the scored target itself, not merely an auxiliary trajectory. The distinguishing condition is observations spanning interior frequencies below and above 1/2 at fixed experimental setting: the child can show faster-than-parent increase at low p but weaker-than-parent increase at high p, or the reverse, with the peak shifted off center. A single refitted parent parameter cannot reproduce such asymmetric shape across those conditions because it only rescales p*(1-p). This refinement remains scientifically admissible because the derivative still must vanish at p=0 and p=1, and the effect is only expected to be visible when data include enough interior range; if observations are confined very near the boundaries, the contrast may be weak.

plan.train_hidden_contrast: In training, the mechanism appears as gradual departure from a single fixed dp_dt-versus-p curve; in holdout, the same history dependence extends to longer times or stronger adaptation, producing additional curvature change not reproducible by one static saturation parameter.
plan.continuation_path: Recover the parent law when the feedback state is frozen or relaxes instantaneously to a constant value equal to the parent frequency_dependence_strength.
plan.promotion_reason: A fixed parameter cannot encode path-dependent changes in the saturation scale. To make dp_dt at the same observed p differ across evolutionary phases under one shared parameter set, the model needs one dynamic state representing accumulated ecological or social feedback.
plan.gap_statement: The current model assumes that the strength of frequency-dependent slowdown is fixed throughout the trajectory, omitting delayed ecological or social feedback that is generated by allele prevalence and then feeds back onto selection.
plan.baseline_assumption: The process already present—frequency-dependent reduction of effective advantage—acts instantaneously with a time-invariant strength parameter.
plan.scientific_mechanism: Accumulation and relaxation of allele-associated crowding, niche depletion, or social interference causes the effective self-limitation experienced by the favored allele to depend on recent history rather than only its instantaneous frequency.
plan.rationale: A realistic next refinement is to relax the parent's instantaneous-feedback assumption rather than adding a new unrelated force. The parent target mapping is single-phase: once p is known, dp_dt is fixed by one static saturating curve. Vary elapsed time along trajectories while holding the initial condition and all fixed parameters the same. Under delayed ecological feedback, two observations with similar interior p but different prior histories can have different dp_dt because inhibitory feedback has had more time to build up or decay. This changes the scored target mapping itself, not only an auxiliary trajectory, because dp_dt for p depends on evolutionary phase. The contrast is scientifically admissible when ecological or social buildup is neither negligible nor infinitely fast relative to allele-frequency change; if adaptation is extremely fast or absent, the child collapses back to the parent. A single refit of the parent parameters cannot reproduce both early weak-slowdown and later strong-slowdown regimes at the same p, because its dp_dt is a unique function of p with fixed curvature for the whole experiment.

The change affects the scored target mapping directly because dp_dt as a function of the supplied states p and q changes; it is not merely a modification of q dynamics. A single parent refit cannot generally absorb this across conditions because it has only one route by which q influences dp_dt, namely the denominator saturation, whereas the child introduces an additional feedback-dependent reshaping of the p-response. contract.assumption_after: The inhibitory factor includes an additional higher-order prevalence term that acts jointly with accumulated feedback q, producing stronger late-stage suppression when the favored allele is common.
contract.observable_signature: For the same supplied p and q, the child preserves near-parent dp_dt when p is small but depresses dp_dt more strongly once p becomes moderate to high, especially when q is appreciable. This is a direct change in the target mapping dp_dt(p,q), not only a change in the auxiliary q trajectory.
contract.shortcut_blocked: A single parent parameter set can only rebalance the existing q*p and q*p**2 contributions, which changes suppression smoothly across all p. It cannot simultaneously keep early-to-mid p growth relatively high while creating an extra late high-p bend tied specifically to the joint state q*p**3; fitting q trajectories alone does not remove this mismatch because the scored derivative is evaluated conditional on the observed p and q.
